caveat: Outlook is an analytical assessment as of October 2026, not a forecast. 2025 figures are IMF estimates/projections.
data_source: IMF World Economic Outlook via DataMapper (latest vintage, accessed October 2026)
debt_management: Czech debt is moderate and on a gently rising trend: 27.6% of GDP in 2006, a low of 27.3% in 2007, 36.9% in 2020 after COVID, and a projected series high of 44.6% in 2025 (42.5% in 2022). The upward drift reflects slower growth and pandemic-era deficits rather than any crisis; by regional standards the stock remains comfortable. GDP grew from $156.2bn in 2006 to a projected $389.0bn in 2025. Debt sustainability is solid, with the government able to borrow cheaply.
inflation_management: The Czech National Bank runs a classic inflation-targeting regime (2% target), and it has faced the sharpest tests of any EU central bank. Inflation was 1% in 2009 and 0.3% in 2015, then surged to 15.1% in 2022, the series high — among the highest in the EU on energy intensity and tight labor markets. The CNB was an early and aggressive hiker, and disinflation was rapid: 2.4% in 2024, projected 2.5% for 2025, back near target. The floating koruna acted as a shock absorber through the cycle.

key_events.event: Global financial crisis; the koruna's float cushioned the adjustment.
CNB exchange-rate floor (2013-2017) fought deflation risk; lifted at 0.3% inflation in 2015.
COVID-19: debt rose to 36.9% of GDP; CNB provided easing.
Inflation surged to 15.1% on energy and labor-market tightness; the CNB led the regional hiking cycle.
Disinflation completed: inflation projected at 2.5%, near the 2% target.

outlook_next_decade: The base case is trend growth around 2% with inflation at target and debt stabilizing under 50% of GDP. Czechia's industrial base faces the energy transition and EV shift as a structural challenge. The koruna's float remains a useful stabilizer, and fiscal consolidation is gradual rather than urgent. The main uncertainty is Germany's industrial cycle, to which Czech output is tightly coupled.
